done_when: In the machine's agent line, a waiting run for an item that other planned work waits on starts before runs nothing waits on, first-come within each group, and its place in line says why. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Test — The adopted-v1.2.2 case rewrites `forge.toml` to the current version and calls `forge sync`; it never runs `forge upgrade`. The test and proof list therefore claim coverage of upgrade plus sync while an upgrade that fails to invoke sync would still pass. The required existing-client upgrade path lacks a test through its real command.
findings.title: Not done: In the machine's agent line, a waiting run for an item that other planned work waits on starts before runs nothing waits on, first

findings.body: Raise: Scale — Every task work, read, or review run calls `board.machine_board(repo)` before entering the machine queue. That command rebuilds repository-wide history and dependency maps and, on a normal repo with open work, requests open and merged pull requests from GitHub. With dozens of planned parts, this cost recurs on every agent run; GitHub latency delays admission even though the queue only needs dependency relationships.
findings.title: Full board and GitHub reads delay task admission

why: The machine's agent line is first-come, so a part other work waits on queues behind new fixes
